It was our Junior year. It was 2007, the spring before the banks shit all over the rest of the country. This happened during the spring semester, so he only had 2 semesters left to graduate. He was wicked smarht, on a full ride academic scholarship.

One week before finals, and we are all studying. Dude is helping us out, he (as usual) has A's in every class. Then, on a Tuesday night, he packs all of his shit into his car, drives home, and doesn't come back. He seemed happy, had a strong socal group of old and new friends, a girl. Just left it all behind. Didn't take any finals, didn't sign up for any more courses, didn't notify the college, nothing. He still had like a 3.2 GPA (after NOT FUCKING TAKING FINALS FOR FIVE CLASSES), so he didn't flunk out. He just quit going.

Now he works at Target doing night shift inventory. He lives in a trailer park. He still seems happy, sociable, has a (different) girl. Volunteers and does the weekend warrior thing. He would never tell any of his "home town" friends (he won't talk to the people he met in college) what happened, and changes the subject if you even bring up college in general. The weirdest part about all of this is that he is one of the two financially secure people in our social circle now. He didn't have any debt from college, he started the job at Target immediately (didn't spend a year or two in an unpaid internship and then looking for a paying position), pays like $250 / month for rent, drives a beater. He's been with Target long enough to get into night inventory management position, so he's bringing home like $50k/year. I know that's not a lot, but he has no loans, no mortgage, no car payment, no kids etc, etc, etc.

It's like he had a vision of the impending financial collapse and was shown a way around it. He has enough money in the bank to purchase a reasonable home outright.
